I'll help analyze the number of different types of chemically equivalent carbon atoms in the compound. Let me check the 13C NMR spectra to count the unique carbon environments.

Looking at the 13C NMR spectra, I can analyze the unique carbon environments:

1. 166.40 ppm - unique signal
2. 144.78 ppm - unique signal
3. 132.00 ppm - unique signal
4. 130.07 ppm - appears twice (equivalent carbons)
5. 127.80 ppm - appears twice (equivalent carbons)
6. 52.24 ppm - unique signal
7. 49.55 ppm - unique signal
8. 43.55 ppm - unique signal
9. 19.23 ppm - unique signal

When counting the number of different types of chemically equivalent carbon atoms (unique carbon environments), we need to count each unique chemical shift only once, even if some shifts appear multiple times due to equivalent carbons.

In this case, we have:
- 7 unique single peaks (166.40, 144.78, 132.00, 52.24, 49.55, 43.55, 19.23)
- 2 peaks that each represent equivalent carbons (130.07, 127.80)

Therefore, there are 9 different types of chemically equivalent carbon atoms.

Final Answer: 9
